packets.requirement: Every word in the final answer must be unique under the frozen normalisation and tokenisation-for-verification rule.
packets.not_covered_deterministically: the abstraction equates distinctness with the token counts agreeing under the frozen tokenisation. Invisible characters no longer defeat it - they are removed before tokenising - but confusables remain outside any automated rule: a Cyrillic look-alike is a different string and NFKC does not merge it, so a projection satisfying this clause can still look to a reader like a repeated word. Section 10.6 assigns homoglyphs to human audit material, not to code
